title: The Richest Americans Get an Extra Decade of Life
hook: Income separates Americans by more years than generations of national progress added.
closing: The income gap is not just comfort; it now maps onto years of American life.
question: Should income predict lifespan?

segments.say: The richest American men outlive the poorest by 14.6 years. Income separates lifespans by more than a decade.
Average American life expectancy rose about nine years across the dataset. That gain is smaller than the income gap shown before.
The richest fifth gained 2.3 years of life. The widening advantage shows the national average hides unequal progress.
